**Gap to close: 0.0562 → 0.0760 (+35%).** HSTU's wins over SASRec come from (a) relative time-bucket attention bias, (b) pointwise silu attention, (c) 100-epoch training on long sequences. Our pipeline literally throws the timestamps away.

## The unused/novel levers

1. **Timestamps (unused signal, big expected gain)** — relative time-bucket attention bias. Prior art exists (TiSASRec 2020; HSTU 2024) so this alone is not novel, but it is the largest expected raw gain and a required ingredient of a competitive recipe.
2. **Text-Anchored Prototype Embeddings (TAPE) — the novelty centerpiece.** TIGER/LIGER show that *shared semantic structure* (semantic IDs) is what scales generative recommenders. We propose the continuous version: k-means the frozen text embeddings into K clusters; compute **frozen soft assignments** A = softmax(text·Cᵀ/τ); add a **learnable prototype table** P (K×d) to each item's feature: e_i = id_emb_i + W·text_i + A_i·P. Items in the same semantic neighborhood share learnable capacity — the TIGER benefit without discrete IDs, without an autoregressive decoder, at near-zero cost. Zero-init P ⇒ exactly recovers the baseline at init (safe).
   - Related work to cite & differentiate: TIGER (discrete RQ-VAE IDs), VQ-Rec (PQ codes), ProtoMF (prototype MF for explainability). Our combination — frozen text-derived soft assignments gating a learnable prototype table inside a sequential recommender — is, to our knowledge, new.
3. **Text-similarity attention bias** — attn(i,j) += w_h · cos(text_i, text_j): inject semantic affinity directly into attention. Light novelty, cheap to test.

## POC protocol (Video_Games = fast iteration: ~8 min/run)

All runs: tuned recipe (d=64, dropout 0.3, warmup-cosine, 50 epochs, chunked-full-softmax), seed 20260608, vs tuned baseline 0.0563 (same seed).

| POC | Flag | Expected | Verdict gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 time bias | `--time-bias` | +3-10% (TiSASRec-magnitude) | keep if > 0.0575 |
| P2 TAPE prototypes | `--text-prototypes 512` | +1-5% | keep if > 0.0570 |
| P3 text-sim bias | `--text-sim-bias` | +0-3% | keep if > 0.0570 |
| P4 combo of winners | combined flags | additive? | — |

Then: 5-seed the winning combo. Success tiers:
- **Tier 1 (likely)**: beat published SASRec 0.0573 → "tuned text+time SASRec beats the SASRec baseline used by HSTU-BLaIR"
- **Tier 2 (uncertain)**: ≥ 0.065 → meaningful step toward HSTU range, strong workshop paper with novel TAPE component
- **Tier 3 (stretch)**: ≥ 0.0760 → SOTA claim vs HSTU-BLaIR

Beauty transfer only after VG verdicts (Beauty runs cost 1.5-2 hrs each).

**Defensible claims**: (1) multi-seed +9.1% over the published SASRec baseline on the HSTU-BLaIR protocol; (2) TAPE (novel) is additive on both softmax and pointwise encoders; (3) Beauty ceiling broken: +17.5% over our pre-campaign baseline; (4) NOT SOTA — published HSTU-BLaIR (0.0760) still leads VG by 17.8% at larger scale; properly attributed throughout.

## Honesty guardrails

- Time-bias alone is NOT claimed as novel (cite TiSASRec, HSTU).
- TAPE is claimed as novel **only after** checking it beats the no-TAPE ablation at ≥2 seeds, and with ProtoMF/TIGER/VQ-Rec cited as related.
- All comparisons to HSTU-BLaIR numbers note: theirs are single-seed, 100-epoch, sampled-softmax-with-local-negatives; ours are 5-seed, 50-epoch, full-softmax.

Best = 0.0637 +/- 0.0003 (5-seed, faithful HSTU + full novel stack + dropout 0.5). +11.1% vs published SASRec 0.0573; -14.1% vs HSTU 0.0741. SOTA 0.0760 ruled INFEASIBLE in this env: reproduced exact recipe on faithful block = 0.0584; their LocalNegativesSampler = uniform random; their eval = full-catalog seen-filtered (= ours); their code needs fbgemm_gpu+torchrec+Triton (Linux-only/sm_120-incompatible). Gap = their CUDA-kernel HSTU numerics. Full evidence in SOTA_VERDICT.md. Novel TAPE adds +8.7% on faithful HSTU. Campaign concluded.

## WSL/sm_120 ceiling-check (2026-06-14) — DEFINITIVE
WSL Ubuntu-20.04 sees the GPU. Installed their pinned torch==2.2.2+cu121. CUDA smoke on device cap (12,0)=sm_120: "CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device". Their CUDA-12.1 stack has NO sm_120 kernels; even in Linux their actual code cannot run on this Blackwell GPU. Running their reference impl would require torch 2.6+/CUDA 12.8 + matching fbgemm_gpu/torchrec/Triton with sm_120 support, which diverges from their pinned reproducible env and likely breaks their code. Path A (run their kernels) = HARDWARE-BLOCKED, proven. Pivoting to novel-architecture probes (C).

- Implemented NOVEL text-distillation aux loss (--text-distill-weight): aligns predicted next-item hidden state with target frozen text emb (1-cosine). Smoke clean. Sweeping w={0.1,0.3,0.5} on best config (faithful HSTU + full stack + dropout 0.5, 40ep) vs 0.0637 baseline.

## 2026-06-15 hourly-loop iteration (2) — c3 result
- **Probe c3 (continuous learnable time-decay kernel) COMPLETE — FAILED, instructive.** L1_decaykernel (best config, --time-bias swapped for --time-decay-kernel K=8, 40ep seed 20260608): best-by-val test NDCG@10=**0.0489** (val 0.0725). The val/test gap is SYSTEMATIC at every eval point — ep10 val0.0668/test0.0463, ep20 0.0702/0.0474, ep30 0.0723/0.0483, ep40 0.0725/0.0489 — a persistent ~0.024 absolute gap vs the bucket time-bias version's ~0.009 (val~0.072/test~0.064). Same times pipeline (bucket version gets test 0.064 on identical data), so the cause is the kernel itself. **Finding: the continuous, sharply-expressive decay kernel OVERFITS the leave-last-out temporal structure** — it attains the single highest validation NDCG of the whole campaign (0.0725) yet the worst test of any time-aware config (0.0489). The bucketed (piecewise-constant) time-bias is the better inductive bias here precisely because it is LESS expressive: it cannot exploit the val-specific last-gap distribution that does not transfer to the test target (which sits one more-recent item further along). More temporal capacity HURTS under LLOO val/test timing shift. Probe c3 is DEAD; bucketed time-bias retained as best. `--time-decay-kernel` left in (default-OFF, zero-init no-op) for the record.

- **Probe c1 (prototype-routed expert value-heads, E=4) COMPLETE — NEUTRAL, failed to gate.** M1_experts4 (best config + --expert-heads 4, 40ep seed 20260608): best-by-val test NDCG@10=**0.0635** (val 0.0723). Diagnosis: the experts route on the SAME frozen level-0 TAPE assignment that the additive prototype table already consumes, so they add redundant capacity over a signal the stack has already saturated. E=8 not attempted — E=4 being exactly neutral (not even marginally positive) indicates the bottleneck is the routing SIGNAL (TAPE clustering, already exploited), not expert count. Probe c1 is DEAD.
- **Probe c4 (2-model score-averaged ensemble) — analytically ruled out for the >0.0760 mandate, not run.** The two strongest base models are HSTU-stack 0.0637 and softmax-stack 0.0578; both < 0.064. A score-averaged ensemble of two models scoring X and Y<X lands between Y and X plus a small diversity bonus (typically +2-5%); the achievable ceiling is ~0.066-0.067, ~13% short of 0.0760. An ensemble cannot leap +20% over its best member. c4 cannot satisfy the mandate by construction, so a GPU cycle is not spent on it (would also require adding a checkpoint-save + dual-load eval harness this script lacks). Documented as ruled-out.

- **W1 (winning stack + LS0.2 + `--niche-share-beta 1.0`, 40ep seed 20260608) COMPLETE — FAILED to gate, DEAD.** Best-by-val test NDCG@10 = **0.0652** (val 0.0735, HR@10 0.1154, n_eval=94,762). vs U2 single-seed 0.0653: **−0.0001** (ties/below); vs U2 5-seed mean 0.0649±0.0002: +0.0003 (within the seed-noise band). - **Decisive interpretable diagnostic — learned β = −7.42 (strongly NEGATIVE, NOT ≈0).** The penalty is `target_scores −= β·log1p(crowd)`; a NEGATIVE β means the model learned to **ADD** to (BOOST), not penalize, the target logit of items in crowded POPULAR semantic niches — i.e. it chose the EXACT OPPOSITE of the ecology fitness-sharing hypothesis. Given a free learnable knob, the stack votes to lean **further INTO** popularity, not away from it. This (a) CONFIRMS the analyst's "popularity over-reliance" diagnosis (ANALYSIS 2026-06-16-1) at the mechanism level, and (b) REFUTES the remedy: explicit inter-item niche competition is the wrong-signed intervention — anti-crowding HURTS, pro-crowding is what the model wants, and even that only buys +0.0003 (noise) because full-catalog NDCG already rewards popular hits, so the converged model had effectively saturated that signal. The first inter-item-interaction term in the ~58-probe campaign is a clean NEGATIVE.
- **Symmetric/eval-side follow-up NOT pursued (correctly):** the proposal permits a symmetric catalog-wide variant ONLY "if β learns a clear POSITIVE sign"; β is clearly NEGATIVE, so the sharing hypothesis is refuted, not merely flat. Moreover applying the niche term at EVAL (β<0 ⇒ up-ranking popular items at scoring time) is exactly the popularity-inflation trap the supervisor's CROSS-FIELD caution flagged — it would inflate the full-catalog number non-defensibly. Declined; no GPU spent on it.

**WHY THE FLOOR, AND THE INFORMATIVE NEXT STEP.** A cold item's representation = (random UNTRAINED ID vector at init-scale) + sbert_proj(frozen text) + TAPE. The large-norm random ID vector likely DOMINATES/corrupts the content signal, pushing cold items to ~random ranks (~1/2458 chance of top-10 => ~0 hits expected). This is exactly the noise conn-gate was meant to remove — but the LEARNABLE gate cannot (no cold gradient). => The genuinely informative tests, both of which sidestep the "no cold gradient" trap, are: (a) a **NON-learnable forced-alpha conn-gate** (force the gate ON for item_users==0, no scalar to vote off) to test the noisy-ID-dominates hypothesis directly; (b) **PROPOSAL 2026-06-23-1 cold-synth** (parameter-free text-kNN aggregation of LEARNED warm-item ID rows — gives the cold item a real collaborative embedding instead of random noise; un-nullable). AND — independent of method — the cold metric must come **off the floor**: re-instrument `by_coldstart` with a COARSER cutoff (NDCG@50/@100 + cold MRR + HR@50) so the arms can actually be distinguished sub-threshold. NDCG@10 cold is uninformative at this catalog density; the @10 null is real but unresolved. **Did NOT 5-seed** — a floored (all-zero) @10 metric cannot produce a non-trivial 5-seed CI; spending 4 more seeds on 0=0 would be wasted GPU. **FIX #1(b) RESOLVED FROM CODE -- cold-synth PARTICIPATES IN TRAINING, it is NOT eval-only.** Traced the call graph in `run_sasrec_sbert.py`:
- `item_features()` (`:724`) applies the cold-synth `torch.where` replacement (`:738-744`) with NO train/eval guard -- it fires on every call. The synthesized vector `synth = (item_emb(nbr) * w).sum(-2)` (`:743`) uses the **LIVE learned `item_emb`** (recomputed each forward), NOT a frozen post-train snapshot; only the neighbor INDICES + softmax WEIGHTS are precomputed once (`:1893-1909`, from frozen SBERT).
- `chunked_full_softmax_loss()` (`:898`, the TRAINING loss) iterates `for start in range(0, n_items, item_chunk)` and calls `model.item_features(chunk_ids)` on EVERY chunk (`:931-934`) -- i.e. over the WHOLE catalog, cold items INCLUDED. Cold items are removed only from training INPUTS and TARGETS (their sequences are stripped), but they remain in the catalog and therefore appear as **NEGATIVE CANDIDATES in the training softmax denominator**.
- MECHANISM: with cold-synth ON, those cold denominator rows change from random-init untrained vectors to populated text-kNN vectors (live sums of warm rows) => the partition function Z changes => the gradient flowing to every warm target's row changes during optimization => warm items end up trained slightly differently => warm/overall eval shifts. This is the leak-free "full-catalog competitor-set effect" the supervisor hypothesized, now LOCATED PRECISELY at **training time** (the softmax denominator, `:934`), not at eval scoring. The old code comment at `:733-737` ("no-op during training, active only at eval scoring") was the ORIGIN of the false claim -- CORRECTED in the code this cycle (`:733-748`).
- Leak-free is intact: no train/val/test target is consulted; synthesis uses only frozen text + learned warm rows; cold items remain valid/test targets only.

⇒ **Removing the untrained random ID row entirely UNLOCKS real cold ranking signal from frozen text (0 → 37 hits@10, 0 → 378 hits@100).** The additive stack's categorical cold=0 is therefore an **ADDITIVE-WIRING artifact** (the untrained random ID row dominates the dot-product `h·e` and buries the frozen-text contribution), **NOT** a fundamental frozen-text insufficiency. The headline negative moves from "observed" to "mechanistically explained": naive additive text-augmentation fails on true cold not because frozen text lacks cold signal, but because the additive architecture cannot surface it past the random ID row.

**HONESTY / caveats (binding framing).** (1) `--sbert-only` is a DIAGNOSTIC, not a deployable method: it discards the entire learned collaborative ID channel, so its OVERALL/warm performance collapses (overall test 0.0116 vs the full V2 MI stack ~0.0413; warm NDCG@10 0.0134). It buys cold signal by sacrificing warm accuracy — the classic content-only cold-start trade, not a free win. (2) Absolute cold NDCG@10 0.00163 (and @100 0.00858) is still ≪ LC2C/z-fusion incumbent ~0.057 — proof-of-mechanism, NOT a cold-start SOTA. (3) Single-seed; NO rel% claim is made. The qualitative finding (categorical 0 → 37/378 hits) is robust to seed noise precisely because the additive baseline is a structural zero, but the ABSOLUTE cold numbers are single-seed and must be 5-seeded before any quantitative claim. (4) This is a mechanism DIAGNOSTIC that clarifies WHY the additive path fails and points the fix (magnitude/wiring of the imputed cold row) — it does NOT itself clear the floor toward LC2C. It complements, does not replace, the cold-synth/norm-restore imputation arms (which keep the warm ID channel intact).

**IMPLICATION for the next run.** This strengthens the EV case for norm-restored cold-synth (2026-06-23-3): the finding that frozen text carries usable cold direction (37 hits@10 without an ID row) is consistent with the norm-restore thesis — cold-synth already injects the right DIRECTION into the cold ID row but caps at ~7–8 hits, plausibly because the kNN-averaged row is norm-CONTRACTED (Jensen) and loses the dot-product magnitude battle. sbert-only's 37 hits (full-magnitude frozen-text projection) vs cold-synth's 7–8 (contracted-magnitude imputed ID row) is CIRCUMSTANTIAL support that magnitude is a binding limiter. Norm-restore is the direct test.

**VERDICT — clean NEGATIVE, redundancy-decorrelation hypothesis REFUTED (pre-registered COLLAPSE-stop fired).** Replacing cold-synth's flat softmax-kNN weights with BLUP/kriging weights `w=(K_ww+λI)⁻¹k_iw` does the OPPOSITE of the thesis: cold COLLAPSES (7 hits@10 → 1; 125 hits@100 → 46) AND drags warm/overall down. **Mechanism — the redundancy the estimator "corrects" is actually SIGNAL here.** Kriging's C⁻¹ term assumes tight near-duplicate neighbor clusters are nuisance double-counting (the geostatistics/GBLUP screening effect, the red-bus/blue-bus IIA failure). But for cold-item text-CF transfer the opposite holds: a zero-interaction cold item's single best collaborative prior IS its near-duplicate franchise/sequel/edition cluster of warm items. BLUP downweights exactly that informative cluster and (via the measured 48% negative-weight mass) pushes the imputed cold ID row toward isolated, noisier neighbors and signed combinations that mis-rank the correct cold target. **The IIA/redundancy failure mode that motivates BLUP in spatial/genomic settings is INVERTED in cold-start CF transfer: near-duplicate text neighbors are the load-bearing signal, not nuisance.**

**WARM/OVERALL DROP — documented competitor-set coupling, NOT a leak (honesty).** Warm −0.0078 / overall −0.0067 exceed the ±0.001 smoke gate, BUT the kriging change is strictly `is_cold`-gated (`torch.where(is_cold, synth, e)`); warm-item eval embeddings are byte-identical given fixed trained weights. The warm shift arises entirely in TRAINING: the cold ID rows are negative candidates in the full-catalog training softmax denominator (`run_sasrec_sbert.py:~934`), and kriging's aggressive signed cold rows (48% neg-mass) perturb warm gradients MORE than cold-synth's gentle contracted average — the SAME mechanism (and same direction/magnitude) that produced norm-restore's −0.0085 warm drop this session. It is a real downstream training effect of bad cold-negatives, not a wiring bug or target leak.

**DECISION (pre-registered, non-fishing).** cold NDCG@100 0.000942 ≪ cold-synth 0.002745 = a measured cold-absolute COLLAPSE ⇒ the proposal's explicit COLLAPSE kill-criterion fired: STOPPED at single-seed (no 5-seed — the 5-seed escalation was gated on a POSITIVE single-seed cold gap, not met), NO nugget sweep (that would re-enter the killed "tune a scalar" axis). The collapse is large and same-signed across @10/@50/@100/MRR/warm/overall, decisive at n=1. NO rel% claim.
